relationship: Manipulating a straight line makes its coordinates, gradient, intercept and equation change together, while testing across the graph distinguishes a genuine relationship from a match at one point.

learnerLoop.action: Manipulate the line, express its properties through working, and test whether it satisfies the challenge.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The line's position or direction changes and its geometric and algebraic descriptions change with it.
learnerLoop.evidence: The graph, coordinates, calculations, feedback and across-the-line test show how well the representations and constraints agree.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Decide which property to adjust, revise the reasoning, or justify that the line satisfies the whole constraint.

invariants: The geometric and algebraic representations describe the same line, so changes in one have coherent consequences in the others.
Learners use evidence across the line, rather than a single visual coincidence, to justify whether a constraint is satisfied.
safeAdaptations: Invent new contexts, values, constraints, manipulatives or challenge sequences that connect straight-line geometry and algebra.
Vary difficulty, scaffolding, working requirements and feedback to suit different learners while preserving meaningful mathematical decisions.
Add alternative representations or ways to test and explain a line relationship, provided their evidence remains mathematically connected.
nonGoals: Expanding into nonlinear graph families unless that comparison directly deepens understanding of straight lines.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

feedback.description: Explains a changing gap, missed mount, incomplete travel or incomplete working.
feedback.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

reference-and-mount.description: Given reference line and, where present, required mounting point P.
reference-and-mount.domain: Cartesian coordinates and line equation; coordinate units.
reference-and-mount.output: Reference equation and coordinate markers remain visible.

candidate-line.description: One candidate line controlled by gradient/intercept, or constant x for a vertical line.
candidate-line.domain: Signed/fractional gradient and intercept; x=k for vertical lines.
candidate-line.source: Learner uses slide/tilt/vertical handles; candidate equation is hidden in Some/All until working conditions allow it.
candidate-line.output: Alignment and changing/constant gap are live geometric evidence.

working-chain.description: Rise/run and m/c are intermediate quantities for ONE line equation. The vertical branch uses dx/k instead.
working-chain.domain: Numeric coordinate differences plus algebraic equation.
working-chain.source: Required keys depend on line type and Working level.
working-chain.output: Each field is checked against the current intended rail geometry.

full-travel-test.description: The carriage samples alignment over the whole required track.
full-travel-test.domain: Position along the bounded test interval.
full-travel-test.source: Learner moves the test carriage after geometry matches.
full-travel-test.output: Visited interval and maximum gap establish whether the alignment holds throughout.

modes.none: Reference and candidate equations/calculations are shown while the learner positions and tests the rail.
modes.some: For nonvertical rails, enter gradient and equation; for vertical rails, enter the equation.
modes.all: Nonvertical: rise, run, gradient, intercept and equation. Vertical: horizontal change, constant k and equation.

dependencies: Correct line placement alone does not complete a rail; the full-travel test remains required.
Required fields must agree with the same setup; changing line geometry invalidates the travel evidence.
Vertical-line working follows x=k rather than an infinite-gradient numeric answer.
implementation.completion: complete() combines geometryOk(), the full travel verification and workingReady(); the popup advances to another rail.
